He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas Longhorns]]. ==High school career== Pittman was a three-year starter at [[B. F. Terry High School]], where he averaged 15 points and 8.5 rebounds per game over his career. In his senior season, he was named the Most Valuable Player for District 24-4A.{{cite news | url=http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/pittman_dexter00.html | title=Dexter Pittman | publisher=[[Texas Longhorns]] | access-date=June 27, 2009 | archive-date=May 23, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130523042723/http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/pittman_dexter00.html | url-status=dead }} Considered a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Pittman was listed as the No. 16 center and the No. 150 player in the nation in 2006.[https://rivals.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Dexter-Pittman-32759;_ylt=AgcJW_CV6TvvYHU6FD2vDf_XO5B4 Dexter Pittman Recruiting Profile] ==College career== Pittman was used sparingly in his first two seasons at Texas, averaging less than 3 points per game with just one start. As a junior, he started 24 games–averaging 10 points and 5.5 rebounds per game{{cite news | url=http://www.texassports.com/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2008-2009/texasmbbstats.html | title=2009 Season Statistics | work=TexasSports | publisher=[[The University of Texas]] | access-date=June 27, 2009}}–and became one of the most dominant centers in the [[Big 12 conference]].{{cite news | url=http://www.big12sports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?PRINTABLE_PAGE=YES&ATCLID=3672855 | title=Texas Student-Athlete Spotlight: Dexter Pittman | publisher=[[Big 12 Conference]] | author=Dan Hurwitz| access-date=June 27, 2009}} ===Weight loss=== Pittman weighed 388 lbs {{cite news | url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/big12/2009-02-10-texas-pittman-cover_N.htm | title=Heavyweight fight has Pittman in shape, ready to roll at Texas | publisher=[[USA Today]] | author=Marlen Garcia | access-date=June 27, 2009 | date=February 11, 2009}} as a senior at Terry High School. After receiving weight loss tips from Texas' Strength and conditioning coach Todd Wright, he was able to drop his weight to 366 lbs before enrolling at Texas. Pittman's weight still prevented him from doing basic drills in practice, which caused various back and knee aches. He dedicated himself to a workout program with Wright including 5:30 a.m. workouts and a complete revamp of his diet. Pittman agreed to call Wright before every meal to evaluate his choices. Pittman later characterized the workout regimen as being so tough that "I wanted to cry and say, 'Man, I want to give up'". Since losing almost 100 pounds, he has become an icon for admirers, like [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Hall of Famer]] [[Charles Barkley]],{{cite news | url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/national/tournament/ncaamen/stories/031909dnspocarltonut.34feb9c.html | title=Pittman's role is now what's huge at Texas | publisher=[[Dallas Morning News]] | author=Chuck Carlton | access-date=June 27, 2009}} who heard about his weight loss. ===College statistics=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | align="left" | [[2006–07 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2006–07]] | align="left" | [[2006–07 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas Longhorns]] | 29 || 0 || 5.3 || .604 || .000 || .471 || 1.8 || .1 || .2 || .3 || 2.6 |- | align="left" | [[2007–08 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2007–08]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2007–08 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas Longhorns]] | '''36''' || 1 || 6.8 || .559 || .000 || .561 || 2.4 || .2 || .1 || .5 || 2.8 |- | align="left" | [[2008–09 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2008–09]] | align="left" | [[2008–09 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas Longhorns]] | 35 || 24 || 16.6 || .616 || .000 || '''.691''' || 5.5 || .4 || '''.4''' || .9 || 10.1 |- | align="left" | [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]] | align="left" | [[2009–10 Texas Longhorns men's basketball team|Texas Longhorns]] | 34 || '''34''' || '''19.1''' || '''.654''' || .000 || .556 || '''5.9''' || '''.5''' || '''.4''' || '''1.9''' || '''10.4''' |- | align="left" | Career | align="left" | | 134 || 59 || 12.2 || .623 || .000 || .601 || 3.9 || .3 || .2 || .9 || 6.6 {{S-end}} ==Professional career== Pittman was selected with the 32nd overall pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]] by the [[Miami Heat]]. On July 16, 2010, he signed a multi-year deal with the Heat. On November 26, 2010, Pittman was assigned to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]. On December 18, 2010, he was recalled by the Heat. On January 6, 2011, he was reassigned to the Skyforce.{{cite web|title=Dexter Pittman Re-Assigned To Sioux Falls Skyforce|url=http://www.nba.com/heat/news/dexter_pittman_reassigned_2011.html|work=NBA.com|access-date=January 23, 2011}} He was selected to the 2011 NBA D-League All-Star game. Pittman made his NBA debut on April 1, 2011, against the Minnesota Timberwolves. The Heat made it to the [[2011 NBA Finals]] but lost to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in six games. On April 13, 2012, Pittman scored a career high 16 points in a 105–82 win against the Charlotte Bobcats. In Game 5 of the 2012 Conference semi-finals against the Indiana Pacers, he was assessed a flagrant foul after he came across the lane and used his forearm to hit [[Lance Stephenson]] of the Pacers with 19.4 seconds left in the game.Tim Reynolds."[http://www.sfltimes.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=10055&Itemid=331 Miami Heat Get Physical]". Associated Press. ''South Florida Times''. May 24, 2012. Retrieved on June 22, 2012. Pittman was later suspended for three games due to the incident."[http://www.hoopsworld.com/heats-haslem-suspended-for-1-game-pittman-for-3 Heat’s Haslem, Pittman suspended]". HoopsWorld. May 24, 2012. Retrieved on June 22, 2012. The Heat advanced to the [[2012 NBA Finals]] and won the series against [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in five games, giving Pittman his first championship. During the 2012–13 season, Pittman was assigned multiple times to the Skyforce.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html 2012-13 NBA Assignments] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140327190108/http://www.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |date=March 27, 2014 }} On February 21, 2013, the Heat traded Pittman and a second round pick to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for a trade exception and the rights to [[Ricky Sanchez]].{{cite news | url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/02/21/heat-grizzlies-trade.ap/index.html | title=Heat send Pittman, draft pick to Grizzlies | work=NBA.com | date=February 21, 2013 | access-date=February 21, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130223034758/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/02/21/heat-grizzlies-trade.ap/index.html | archive-date=February 23, 2013 | url-status=dead }} On April 14, 2013, he was waived by the Grizzlies.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/04/14/grizzlies-waive-dexter-pittman.ap/index.html |title=Grizzlies waive Dexter Pittman |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=April 15, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130627012438/http://www.nba.com/2013/news/04/14/grizzlies-waive-dexter-pittman.ap/index.html |archive-date=June 27, 2013 |url-status=dead }} Pittman joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]].[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/130709_las_vegas_summer_league_roster Spurs Announce 2013 Las Vegas Summer League Roster] In September 2013, he signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14338 |title=Patrick Christopher, Mike James, Dahntay Jones, Kalin Lucas, Dexter Pittman and D.J. White in Bulls training camp |access-date=September 28, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029191020/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14338 |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |url-status=dead }} However, he was later waived by the Bulls on October 26, 2013.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14655 |title=Chicago Bulls waive Dexter Pittman, D.J. White |access-date=October 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029195950/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14655 |archive-date=October 29, 2013 |url-status=dead }} On November 27, 2013, Pittman was acquired by the [[Springfield Armor]]. However, his contract was bought out by the Armor on December 3, before he appeared in a game for them. He then signed with the [[Foshan Dralions|Foshan Long Lions]] of China as an injury-replacement for [[Shavlik Randolph]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.asiancagers.com/nba-center-dexter-pittman-will-replace-injured-shavlik-randolph-in-foshan/ |title=CBA: NBA Center Dexter Pittman will Replace Injured Shavlik Randolph in Foshan |access-date=October 29, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029115448/http://www.asiancagers.com/nba-center-dexter-pittman-will-replace-injured-shavlik-randolph-in-foshan/ |archive-date=October 29, 2014 |url-status=dead }} Later that month, he left Foshan after seven games. On January 6, 2014, Pittman was acquired by the Austin Toros.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/austin/austin_toros_acquire_dexter_pi_2014_01_06.html Austin Toros Acquire Dexter Pittman In Trade] On February 22, 2014, Pittman signed a 10-day contract with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-dexter-pittman-10-day-contract HAWKS SIGN DEXTER PITTMAN TO 10-DAY CONTRACT] Pittman's final NBA game was on February 26, 2014, in a 104–115 loss to the Boston Celtics. In that game, Pittman only played 30 seconds and didn't record a single statistic. On February 27, 2014, he was waived by the Hawks.[http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-release-dexter-pittman HAWKS RELEASE DEXTER PITTMAN] On March 2, 2014, he was reacquired by the Toros.
